start_here: Say to your AI: "Add my Spring menu draft (https://example.com/menu/spring) to my Notion database 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef with the note 'Check prices before we print.'" It runs tool:add-to-notion and makes the page.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it takes the things and note it is given and posts them once to the person's connected service.
instructions: 1. Connect Notion in your Trillion account (service_connection:notion) and share the target database with that integration.
2. Copy the database id: the 32 letters and numbers in the database's address.
3. Say to your AI the start_here sentence; it calls tools:run for tool:add-to-notion with things, note, database and optional title.
4. Read $.said (it must say answered with the status) and open the new page in Notion to see the note and the link.

worked_examples.title: Add a picked note to a Notion database
worked_examples.ask: Add a picked note to a Notion database
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/send-to-a-place/tool-rows.json (the row's invoke body) and checked against tools/send-to-a-place/test/send-to-a-place-rows.test.mjs: the person has connected Notion (service_connection:notion). The body makes a page in database 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef titled "Spring menu review", with a paragraph holding the note and a paragraph linking "Spring menu draft" to https://example.com/menu/spring. I could not run it: it needs a live Notion token, so the answer is worked out from the row, and the exact "said" wording follows the webhook sibling's pattern "<host> answered <status>".
worked_examples.hands_back: {"status":200,"said":"api.notion.com answered 200","answer":"<Notion's page object as text>"}: the verify step requires $.said to contain "answered". With no title the page is titled with things.0.label.
